sanskrit: hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayaḥ pāvakā yāsu jātaḥ kaśyapo yāsv indraḥ | yā agniṃ garbhaṃ dadhire suvarṇās tā na āpaḥ śaṃ syonā bhavantu ||
english: Golden-hued, pure, purifying — those waters in which Kaśyapa was born, in which Indra was born; those golden ones that held Agni as an embryo — may those waters be auspicious and gentle to us.

sanskrit: yāsāṃ rājā varuṇo yāti madhye satyānṛte avapaśyañ janānām | (…) ||
english: Those waters through whose midst King Varuṇa moves, beholding the truth and falsehood of men — [the remainder of the verse is not preserved in this recension].

sanskrit: yāsāṃ devā divi kṛṇvanti bhakṣaṃ yā antarikṣe bahudhā bhavanti | yā agniṃ garbhaṃ dadhire suvarṇāḥ (…) ||
english: Those waters of which the gods in heaven partake as their drink, which become manifold in the atmosphere; those golden ones that held Agni as an embryo — [the remainder is not preserved in this recension].

sanskrit: śivena mā cakṣuṣā paśyatāpaḥ śivayā tanvopa spṛśata tvacaṃ me | ghṛtaścutaḥ śucayo yāḥ pāvakās tā na āpaḥ śaṃ syonā bhavantu ||
english: O waters, look upon me with a benign eye; touch my skin with your benign body. Those that drip with clarified butter, pure, purifying — may those waters be auspicious and gentle to us.

sanskrit: suparṇo jātaḥ prathamas tasya tvaṃ pittam āsitha | tad āsurī yudhā jītā rūpaṃ cakre vanaspatīn ||
english: When the Suparṇa-bird was first born, you were its bile. That which the Āsurī-woman, having conquered it in battle, fashioned into a form — she fashioned it among the forest-trees.

sanskrit: āsurī cakre prathamā- -idaṃ kilāsabheṣajam idaṃ kilāsanāśanam | anīnaśat kilāsaṃ sarūpām akarat tvacam ||
english: The Āsurī-woman was the first to prepare this remedy for leucoderma, this destroyer of leucoderma. She made the leucoderma vanish; she rendered the skin of uniform color.

sanskrit: sarūpā nāma te mātā sarūpo nāma te pitā | sarūpakṛt tvam oṣadhe sā sarūpam idaṃ kṛdhi ||
english: Sarūpā is the name of your mother, Sarūpa is the name of your father. You, O herb, are a maker of uniform color — make this person of uniform color.

sanskrit: yat tanūjaṃ yad agnijaṃ citraṃ kilāsaṃ jajñiṣe | tad astu sutvak tanvo yatas tvāpanayāmasi ||
english: Whatever variegated leucoderma has arisen from the body, whatever has arisen from Agni — may that become healthy skin on the body, since we are removing it from you.

sanskrit: śyāmā sarūpaṃkaraṇī pṛthivyā adhy udbhṛtā | idam ū ṣu pra sādhaya punā rūpāṇi kalpaya ||
english: The dark herb that makes uniform color, uplifted from the earth — accomplish this very task now; restore the proper hues again.

sanskrit: abhayaṃ somaḥ savitā kṛṇotv abhayaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī ubhe | abhayaṃ svar antarikṣaṃ no astu saptaṛṣīṇāṃ haviṣābhayaṃ no 'stu ||
english: May Soma and Savitṛ grant us freedom from fear; may both Heaven and Earth grant us freedom from fear. May the sky and the atmosphere be without fear for us; through the oblation of the Seven Seers may there be freedom from fear for us.

sanskrit: abhayaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī ihāstu no agnināmitrān praty oṣataṃ pratīcaḥ | mā jñātāraṃ mā pratiṣṭhāṃ vidanta mitho vighnānā upa yantu mṛtyum ||
english: May Heaven and Earth be without fear for us here; O Agni, burn back the foes facing us. May they not find our kinsman, may they not find our stronghold; wounding one another, may they go to death.

sanskrit: pañca devā abhayasyeśata indras tvaṣṭā varuṇo mitros agniḥ | māyaṃ grāmo duritam ena ārad anyatra rājñām abhi yātu manyuḥ ||
english: Five gods are lords of freedom from fear: Indra, Tvaṣṭṛ, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni. May no calamity, no sin come near this village; may the wrath of the kings pass elsewhere.

sanskrit: asmai grāmāya pradiśaś catasra ūrjaṃ subhūtaṃ savitā dadhātu | aśatrum indro abhayaṃ kṛṇotu madhye ca viśāṃ sukṛte syāma ||
english: May Savitṛ bestow upon this village from all four directions vigor and good prosperity. May Indra render it free of enemies and free from fear; may we be among the well-doing folk in the midst of the community.
